questions.question: What character rules and length constraints apply to custom_alias?
options: Base62 characters only [0-9a-zA-Z], length 3-32
URL-safe characters including hyphen/underscore, length 1-64
No restriction beyond URL-path safety
questions.default_if_unanswered: Base62 characters only [0-9a-zA-Z], length 3-32; violations return 400 problem+json

questions.question: How should a POST be treated when the same long_url was already shortened (no custom_alias)? The spec says 'resource already exists -> 409' — does that apply to duplicate long_urls or only to taken aliases?
options: 409 only for taken custom_alias; duplicate long_urls get a new distinct short code
409 for duplicate long_url by the same creator
Return 200/201 with the existing short_url (idempotent)
questions.default_if_unanswered: 409 only applies to taken custom_alias; posting the same long_url again creates a new distinct short code

questions.question: What URL validation rules apply to long_url (allowed schemes, max length)?
options: Only http/https, max 2048 characters
Any syntactically valid absolute URI, max 8192 characters
http/https plus ftp, no length limit
questions.default_if_unanswered: Only http and https schemes, maximum 2048 characters; otherwise 400 problem+json

questions.question: Since authentication is a non-goal, how should the created_by column be populated?
options: Nullable and left null
Populated from an optional request header (e.g., X-Created-By) if present, else null
Fixed constant such as 'anonymous'
questions.default_if_unanswered: Nullable column left null in this scenario

questions.question: Should an expiration_date in the past (or invalid ISO-8601 value) be rejected at creation time?
options: Reject both past and malformed values with 400
Reject malformed values with 400 but accept past dates (link is immediately 410)
Accept anything parseable, silently ignore invalid values
questions.default_if_unanswered: Reject both malformed ISO-8601 and past expiration_date values with 400 problem+json

questions.question: How should Redis unavailability affect the read path (cache miss handling)?
options: Bypass cache and serve directly from Postgres, degrade gracefully
Return 503 if Redis is down
Serve from Postgres and asynchronously retry cache population
questions.default_if_unanswered: Bypass the cache and serve redirects directly from Postgres, logging the degradation

questions.question: How are read-path and write-path separations enforced — should each instance disable the other path's endpoints?
options: Profiles conditionally register only the relevant controllers; other endpoints return 404
All endpoints available on all instances; separation is routing/infrastructure concern only
A single 'all' profile plus dedicated read/write profiles
questions.default_if_unanswered: Spring profiles (read, write, plus a default combined profile) conditionally register controllers; a read instance returns 404 for write endpoints and vice versa

questions.question: What is the short_url base domain/host returned in the response?
options: Configurable base URL property (e.g., app.base-url) with a localhost default
Derived from the incoming request's Host header
Hardcoded placeholder domain
questions.default_if_unanswered: Configurable base URL application property, defaulting to http://localhost:8080
